standard_prerequisites.name: Completions as inverse limits over a fundamental system of open submodules, and exactness of inverse limits of short exact sequences
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces exactness of the completions to exactness of the quotients.

standard_prerequisites.name: The canonical map from a module to its completion has dense image, and the kernel of the induced map on completions is closed
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the completion of the submodule with the closure of the image.

core_obligations: Choose a fundamental system of open submodules of M, note that its intersections with N and its images in M/N are fundamental systems, and reduce exactness of the completions to exactness of the short exact sequences of quotients and the commutativity of limits with limits (proof lines 959-967).

Identify the completion of N with the closure of its image in the completion of M, using density of the image of N in its completion and closedness of the kernel of the map between completions (proof lines 967-969).
proof_roadmap: The closure of the image (proof lines 967-969).
difficulty_reason: For a submodule N of a linearly topologized module M over a topological ring, the lemma asserts that the sequence of completions from the completion of N to the completion of M to the completion of the quotient is exact, and that the completion of N is the closure of the image of N in the completion of M (statement lines 947-957). The proof chooses a fundamental system of open submodules of M and records that its intersections with N and its images in the quotient are fundamental systems there, so exactness reduces to the exactness of the evident short exact sequences of quotients together with the fact that limits commute with limits (proof lines 959-967). The second assertion is then derived from the first: the canonical map from N to its completion has dense image and the kernel of the map between the completions is closed, so it equals the closure of that image (proof lines 967-969). The claim is H2: the reduction to quotients and the passage to limits are carried out explicitly, and the second part is a short consequence of the first with its two supporting facts named.
